# libtmux for Ruby Create tmux sessions, split windows, send input, and capture pane output from Ruby. Read server state into a [snapshot][snapshot], then query it with [`where`][selection-where], [`select`][selection-select], and the rest of `Enumerable`. [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Find things](#find-things-in-a-snapshot) · [Packages](#packages) · [Guide](docs/index.md) · [API reference](docs/reference/api.md) · [Recipes](docs/recipes.md) · [API on libtmux.org](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/) [![compatibility](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/actions/workflows/compatibility.yml) [![libtmux](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux?label=libtmux)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/LICENSE)
Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and each release increments `N`. The API is not settled: any release may change or remove exported identifiers, and the changelog of each gem marks its breaks. Pin an exact version to avoid one. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), which links each gem's own, and the [release guide](docs/releasing.md). It suits scripts, tests that need a real tmux, and tools that drive a terminal program. An [MCP server][mcp-application], an Async adapter and a workspace loader ship beside the core, under [Packages](#packages). **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Find things](#find-things-in-a-snapshot) · [Your own server](#use-the-tmux-server-you-already-run) · [Packages](#packages) · [Build from source](#build-from-source) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the core gem from RubyGems. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer on `PATH`: ```console $ gem install libtmux ``` This program creates a session, adds a window, splits it, and prints each window with its panes. [`Server.start`][server-start] closes its private tmux server when the block exits, and the snapshot stays readable afterward: ```ruby require "libtmux" snapshot = LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.snapshot end snapshot.windows.each do |window| puts "#{window.name}: #{window.panes.map(&:id).join(', ')}" end ``` From a checkout, run the [complete example](examples/quickstart.rb): ```console $ mise exec -- bundle exec ruby examples/quickstart.rb ``` It prints: ```text main: %0 logs: %1, %2 ``` Pane commands take argument arrays. [`Server.start`][server-start] gives its tmux server a socket and an empty configuration of its own, so it never touches a tmux you already use. ## Find things in a snapshot ### [`Server#snapshot`][server-snapshot]: one read, many queries Continue with the snapshot above. [`where`][selection-where] accepts criteria as data, and [`select`][selection-select] accepts a Ruby block. These queries make no tmux calls: ```ruby panes = snapshot.panes active_ids = panes.where(active: true).map(&:id) wide_panes = panes.select { |pane| pane.width >= 40 } panes_by_window = panes.group_by { |pane| pane.window.name } logs = snapshot.windows.one(name: "logs") missing = snapshot.windows.one_or_nil(name: "missing") ``` [`one`][selection-one] raises [`NoMatchError`][nomatcherror] or [`MultipleMatchesError`][multiplematcheserror] unless exactly one record matches. [`one_or_nil`][selection-one_or_nil] returns `nil` for no match and still rejects duplicates. Both errors live under `LibTmux`. A selection keeps the membership it captured. Call [`server.snapshot`][server-snapshot] again while the server is open to read later changes. The [field catalog][doc-fields] lists query fields and wire names, and the [list/filter recipe](examples/list_filter.rb) covers exact matches and queries after close. ## Use the tmux server you already run ### [`Server.new`][server-new]: borrow a daemon [`Server.open`][server-open] and [`Server.new`][server-new] bind an endpoint that already exists, such as `Server.open(socket_path: ...)`. Closing the binding leaves the daemon running. The outer [`Server.start`][server-start] block here only supplies a daemon to borrow: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |owner| owner.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server = LibTmux::Server.new(endpoint: owner.endpoint) begin puts "connected sessions: #{server.list_sessions.length}" ensure server.close end puts "sessions after client close: #{owner.list_sessions.length}" end ``` It prints: ```text connected sessions: 1 sessions after client close: 1 ``` See [ownership and errors][doc-ownership] for what close and failure mean. ## Packages Start with `libtmux`. Add the companion for your caller: | Gem | Require | Use it for | | --- | --- | --- | | [libtmux](gems/libtmux/README.md) | `libtmux` | Blocking scripts, snapshots, and control connections | | [libtmux-async](gems/libtmux-async/README.md) | `libtmux/async` | Concurrent commands and bounded streams in Async tasks [![libtmux-async](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-async?label=libtmux-async)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async) | | [libtmux-mcp](gems/libtmux-mcp/README.md) | `libtmux/mcp` | An MCP server with explicit endpoints and tool policy [![libtmux-mcp](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-mcp?label=libtmux-mcp)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) | | [libtmux-workspace](gems/libtmux-workspace/README.md) | `libtmux/workspace` | YAML/JSON workspace plans and a CLI to apply them [![libtmux-workspace](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-workspace?label=libtmux-workspace)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace) | Requiring a gem starts no tmux process, scheduler, or protocol server. The companion gems install separately. [Execution modes][doc-modes] explains blocking calls, Async tasks, and control subscriptions. ### [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux): the core Blocking [server][server], [session][session], [window][window] and [pane][pane] handles, immutable [snapshots][snapshot], and [control connections][controlconnection]. Require `libtmux`. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) ```console $ gem install libtmux ``` The [quick start](#quick-start) and [snapshot queries](#find-things-in-a-snapshot) above run against this gem. ### [libtmux-async](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-async): concurrent commands Concurrent commands and bounded control streams inside an Async task that your application owns. Require `libtmux/async`, then open a scope with [`LibTmux::Async.open`][async-open]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/libtmux-async/) · [Guide](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/async/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async) ```console $ gem install libtmux-async ``` Capture every pane concurrently with [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]. This excerpt uses an open [`LibTmux::Server`][server] and the `Example.check` assertion helper from the [complete program](examples/async_cancel.rb): ```ruby Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| refs = scope.server.list_panes.map(&:ref) screens = scope.map(refs, concurrency: 2) { |ref| scope.server.pane(ref).capture } Example.check(screens.length == refs.length && screens.all?(&:success?), "concurrent captures failed") end end.wait ``` ### [libtmux-mcp](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-mcp): a tmux server for MCP clients An MCP server over stdio for one tmux server, with an explicit tool policy. Installs `libtmux-mcp`; require `libtmux/mcp` to embed it through [`LibTmux::MCP::Application`][mcp-application]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/reference/) · [Tools](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) ```console $ gem install libtmux-mcp ``` The server borrows a tmux server that is already running. Start one on a socket of its own: ```console $ tmux -L agent new-session -d -s work ``` Add the server to Claude Code. Until you enable more tools, it serves [`tmux_capabilities`][tool-tmux_capabilities] and [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: ```console $ claude mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp --socket-name agent --endpoint dev ``` The [MCP README](gems/libtmux-mcp/README.md) covers other clients, every tool and authored shell commands. Tracked captures, waits and authored runs need tmux 3.3a or newer and native process identity. ### [libtmux-workspace](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-workspace): YAML workspaces YAML or JSON workspaces, validated, planned offline and applied to an open server. Installs `libtmux-workspace`; require `libtmux/workspace` to use it from Ruby through [`LibTmux::Workspace`][workspace]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/reference/) · [Command reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/cli/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace) ```console $ gem install libtmux-workspace ``` Save this workspace as `workspace.yaml`: ```yaml session_name: work environment: PROJECT_MODE: development windows: - window_name: editor window_index: 1 layout: tiled panes: - shell_command: printf 'editor ready\n' - {} ``` Check it without contacting tmux: ```console $ libtmux-workspace validate workspace.yaml ``` ```text Workspace configuration is valid. ``` The [workspace README](gems/libtmux-workspace/README.md) loads it into a running server and lists every option, including how `--switch` moves a client. ## Build from source Use the Ruby pinned in [.tool-versions](.tool-versions) and have `tmux` on your `PATH`. From this checkout, install the development bundle: ```console $ mise install ``` ```console $ mise exec -- bundle config set --local path vendor/bundle ``` ```console $ mise exec -- bundle install ``` To use the core outside this checkout, build the artifacts: ```console $ mise exec -- bundle exec rake build ``` Install into the Ruby environment that will run your application. The core's runtime dependencies must already be installed for this local-only command: ```console $ gem install \ --local \ --no-document \ pkg/libtmux-0.1.1.gem ``` Companion gems need their declared runtime dependencies too. The [packaging check](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#checks) verifies each gem in an isolated installation and runs the recipes outside the checkout. ## What it leaves out - **Live objects.** A [snapshot][snapshot] record is what tmux said when you read it, and a selection keeps the membership it captured. Read again to see a change. - **A terminal emulator.** [`Pane#capture`][pane-capture] returns what tmux's `capture-pane` prints for the pane. - **A server it starts on its own.** [`Server.new`][server-new] and [`Server.open`][server-open] bind a running server and never start one. With no socket named, [`Endpoint.new`][endpoint-new] picks the one tmux would: `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, `LIBTMUX_SOCKET`, the server `TMUX` names, then tmux's default socket. The recipes name a socket or own one. - **Whole-program typing.** RBS declarations ship with each gem, and selected installed calls are checked. See the [public methods][doc-api]. - **Throughput claims.** The [benchmarks][doc-benchmark] list their workloads, measurements and limits. ## Support and status Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and each release increments `N`. The API is not settled: any release may change or remove exported identifiers, and the changelog of each gem marks its breaks. Pin an exact version to avoid one. - **Ruby 3.3 or newer** and **tmux 3.3a or newer.** Unpatched 3.3 is below the minimum. A [server handle][server] checks the connected daemon's release, not the client's, and refuses an older daemon before any requested command runs. tmux release candidates are not supported: a feature can require one only until its release ships, and a candidate such as `X.Y-rcN` ranks below `X.Y`. See [Release candidates][rc-policy]. - **Linux, including WSL, and macOS.** The [compatibility workflow][compat] runs Ruby 3.3, 3.4 and 4.0 with tmux 3.3a through 3.8 on Ubuntu 24.04. A push and a pull request run the oldest and newest of those releases, 3.3a and 3.8, and a release runs all of them. macOS is supported on a best-effort basis, and CI coverage for it is highly limited. - **Control connections need tmux 3.7 or newer.** On an older daemon `open_control` raises `UnsupportedFeatureError` before a client attaches, and `Server#supports_control?` returns false. Other optional features carry their own releases in the [optional-feature table][doc-optional-features]; [`capabilities.json`][capabilities-json] holds the same records for tools. - **tmux master and old daemons.** On Ubuntu the workflow also runs the suite against a pinned tmux master, and checks that tmux 3.0a, 3.1c, 3.2a and 3.3 daemons are refused. - **Per-revision results.** Check the workflow's results for your revision before relying on one combination. ## Documentation - [Send text and capture output](examples/layout_io.rb): split panes, wait for output events, and round-trip binary buffers. - [Work with linked windows](examples/window_links.rb): address one window at several session indexes. - [Capture concurrently](examples/async_cancel.rb): read panes while another request waits, then cancel it. - [Load a workspace](examples/workspace_apply.rb): parse a configuration, plan, and apply it. - [All recipes](docs/recipes.md): cancellation, control streams, command groups, and MCP. - [API reference](docs/reference/api.md): public methods, source links, and behavioral contracts. # Execution modes

| Mode | Wait and ownership | Result evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core command | Calling thread blocks; server binding owns each client and its pipes | `CommandResult` has binary stdout/stderr and final client status |
| Captured query | Snapshot acquisition performs explicit I/O; `Selection` filtering is local | Stable captured membership with acquisition interval and coverage |
| Command group | One client submits an ordered, nontransactional group | Aggregate final status; individual steps remain `unknown` |
| Core control | One owned reader thread drains the connection; each subscriber has limits | Guarded blocks between boundaries; hooks can share the interval |
| Async | Caller supplies an Async parent task; pipe I/O yields on its scheduler | Same command evidence, with bounded request admission and cancellation |
| MCP | Caller supplies transport streams, Async scope and tool policy | Versioned protocol envelopes and structured tool responses |
| Workspace | Parsing and planning are inert; apply performs ordered commands | Created-reference ledger, observed effects and explicit uncertainty |

Use `Server.open(socket_path: ...)` to borrow a daemon through a pinned
binding. With no socket named, `Server.open` borrows the daemon tmux would pick
(see [Endpoints](reference/behavior.md#endpoints)). `Server.start` creates an
owned daemon on a unique socket and closes it with the block. These recipes
name a socket or own one.

`CommandResult#success?` means the client exited successfully. Sending input
does not establish shell completion. A `GuardedReply` has no `success?`:
`%end` terminates a guard, while WAIT commands, aliases and hooks can change
what finishes when. Its `boundary_window` attribution is deliberately weaker
than per-command ownership.

Concurrent control calls pipeline complete wire requests on one connection.
The writer can submit a later request while an earlier reply waits; the reader
assigns boundaries in the same order. Admission limits include all pending
and completed but unconsumed requests. Cancellation after any request bytes
are written closes the connection: other written requests have
`possibly_sent` delivery, and requests with no written bytes have `not_sent`.
No uncertain request is replayed. Sequential calls still wait for each reply.

Reliable control subscriptions raise `SubscriptionOverflow` when they cannot
retain the stream. Tail subscriptions emit a gap containing lost sequence
and byte evidence. Neither mode blocks the command reader behind a slow
consumer. Limits apply to connection-owned buffers; callers own the replies
they retain after return.

Captured queries evaluate the whole criteria tree before selecting rows,
including inactive OR branches. Explain methods perform no I/O. Current
source plans use explicit capture and local evaluation; unsupported required
pushdown fails rather than silently changing semantics.

See [the recipes](recipes.md) for event-based WAIT release, cancellation,
overflow and group-failure examples. No throughput comparison is claimed.

# Ownership and errors

An entity reference contains a binding identity, kind and tmux-assigned ID.
Window links also retain session and index context. A snapshot can describe
one window at several indexes without creating several window identities.
Names are query values, not substitutes for stable command targets.

A borrowed binding retains its private socket route. Replacing the public
socket does not authorize following a new server. Closing the binding retires
owned clients and pipes and preserves the borrowed daemon. A server started
with `Server.start` owns its daemon and temporary directory as well. Handles,
Async tasks and subscriptions cannot be transferred to another process or
scheduler as if their ownership were unchanged.

| Failure or empty value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Empty `Selection` / `one_or_nil` returns `nil` | A valid complete local selection has no matching record |
| `NoMatchError` / `MultipleMatchesError` | `one` cannot establish exactly one match |
| `InvalidFilterError` / `FieldDecodeError` | Criteria or wire values do not satisfy the declared schema |
| `IncompleteSnapshotError` | Required coverage is unavailable; do not infer absence |
| `TargetNotFoundError` | The guarded target no longer matches its identity/context |
| `Cancelled` / `DeadlineExceeded` | The requested wait ended; delivery evidence determines possible effects |
| `SubscriptionOverflow` / gap event | A bounded stream cannot establish uninterrupted delivery |
| `Workspace::ApplyError` | Inspect its immutable result ledger before deciding whether to compensate |

Operation errors report a phase and delivery evidence: `not_sent`,
`possibly_sent`, or `observed`. An observed nonzero exit still needs its
command result. Cleanup diagnostics accompany failures; cleanup failure is
not a successful close. A cancelled mutating request can already have effects.
A timed-out WAIT lock request can still acquire its queued remote lock after
a later unlock; retiring the client does not roll back tmux's command queue.

Client cancellation sends TERM, then KILL if exit is still unobserved, and
uses the remaining cleanup deadline to reap the owned child. There is no
scheduled grace period for a TERM handler. This policy applies to owned
command clients; cancelling their requests does not terminate borrowed panes
or daemons.

Create `LibTmux::Cancellation.new` for blocking requests and pass it as `cancel:`.
Calling `cancel` from another thread wakes current users of that token and makes
`cancelled?` true permanently; later requests with the same token refuse before
dispatch. A token can cancel several requests. It owns a pipe, starts no thread,
and must remain open until every request using it has returned. Join those
callers before calling `close`; closing a token does not join them. Both methods
are idempotent and their return values are unspecified. `reader` belongs to the
token: do not consume its bytes or close it separately. After a fork, a child
may close its inherited descriptors but cannot query or cancel the parent's token.
The [plain-Ruby example](../examples/cancel.rb) proves wakeup, delivery evidence
and client reaping without sleeps. Async tasks can instead use `Task#cancel` as
shown in the [Async example](../examples/async_cancel.rb).

Workspace compensation is explicit. It removes only a positively created
session whose current windows and panes all belong to the creation ledger,
checked in the same tmux command turn. A borrowed window or pane moved into
that session prevents destructive compensation. Arbitrary shell effects
cannot be rolled back, and an unacknowledged creation is never guessed by name.

Parsing errors and ordinary inspection redact payloads. Explicit results,
captures, plans and canonical exports contain the requested data, including
commands or normalized paths; callers control their storage and display.

See [execution modes](modes.md) and [workspace details](../gems/libtmux-workspace/README.md).

# Executable recipes

Every linked program loads installed gems, starts an isolated server, asserts
its result and verifies owned-daemon cleanup. The shared
[support module](../examples/support.rb) supplies assertions and the cleanup
wrapper. No program adds checkout paths to Ruby's load path.

Run a program from the repository after installing its required local gems:

```console
$ ruby examples/window_links.rb
```

The artifact suite copies programs outside the checkout and runs them against
each gem's isolated dependency closure. [The manifest](../examples/manifest.json)
owns file discovery and the source regions used below. `scripts/examples
--check` rejects an unlisted program or a changed excerpt.

## Captured queries

[Complete list/filter/exact-one program](../examples/list_filter.rb). A fresh
window does not alter an existing capture; local filtering still works after
the binding closes.

<!-- example: list_filter/main -->
```ruby
session = server.new_session(name: "capture", command: ["/bin/cat"])
session.new_window(name: "second", command: ["/bin/cat"])
snapshot = server.snapshot
panes = snapshot.panes
first = panes.one(id: panes.first.id)
session.new_window(name: "later", command: ["/bin/cat"])
Example.check(panes.size == 2, "captured membership changed")
Example.check(panes.where(id: first.id).one.ref == first.ref, "wrong exact match")
Example.raises(LibTmux::MultipleMatchesError) { panes.one }
Example.check(panes.one_or_nil(id: "%4294967294").nil?, "missing pane was invented")
```
<!-- /example -->

## Layout and bytes

[Complete layout/capture/send program](../examples/layout_io.rb). On tmux 3.7
and newer a control output event establishes that the literal input has
reached the pane before capture; older daemons refuse the control client.
Binary buffers round-trip without text decoding.

<!-- example: layout_io/main -->
```ruby
receipt = server.new_session(name: "layout", command: ["/bin/cat"], receipt: true)
pane = receipt.pane
second = pane.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"])
receipt.window.select_layout("tiled")
Example.check(receipt.window.list_panes.map(&:id).sort == [pane.id, second.id].sort, "assigned pane IDs differ")
if Example.control?(server)
  server.open_control(session: receipt.entity.ref) do |control|
    control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 0.5)
    output = control.subscribe(pane_id: pane.id, max_bytes: 8192, max_events: 32)
    literal = "literal; #{'#{pane_id}'} $HOME"
    pane.send_text(literal)
    bytes = "".b
    bytes << output.next(timeout: 0.5).data until bytes.include?(literal)
    Example.check(pane.capture.stdout.include?(literal), "capture lost literal input")
  end
else
  Example.refuses_control(server, receipt.entity)
end
payload = "NUL\0\xff\n".b
server.write_buffer(name: "bytes", data: payload)
Example.check(server.read_buffer("bytes").stdout == payload, "buffer bytes changed")
```
<!-- /example -->

## One window at three indexes

[Complete window-link program](../examples/window_links.rb). Window identity
and selection context remain distinct.

<!-- example: window_links/main -->
```ruby
session = server.new_session(name: "links", command: ["/bin/cat"])
window = session.list_windows.fetch(0)
session.link_window(window.ref, index: 4)
session.link_window(window.ref, index: 9)
links = session.list_window_links
Example.check(links.map(&:index) == [0, 4, 9], "link indexes differ")
Example.check(links.map { |link| link.window.ref }.uniq == [window.ref], "window identity split")
Example.check(links.map(&:ref).uniq.length == 3, "link contexts collapsed")
links.find { |link| link.index == 9 }.select
Example.check(session.display('#{window_index}').text == "9\n", "wrong current link")
```
<!-- /example -->

## Blocking request cancellation

[Complete plain-Ruby cancellation program](../examples/cancel.rb). A tmux event
proves dispatch before another thread cancels the blocked client. The program
joins the caller, checks client reaping and closes the token's owned pipe.

<!-- example: cancel/main -->
```ruby
cancellation = LibTmux::Cancellation.new
waiting = nil
begin
  waiting = Thread.new do
    server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"],
      timeout: 0.5, cancel: cancellation)
  rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error
    error
  end
  server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 0.5)
  cancellation.cancel
  failure = waiting.value
  Example.check(failure.is_a?(LibTmux::Cancelled), "cancellation lost")
  Example.check(failure.delivery == :possibly_sent, "dispatched wait claimed no effects")
  Example.raises(Errno::ECHILD) { Process.waitpid(failure.pid, Process::WNOHANG) }
  Example.check(server.diagnostics.fetch(:admitted_requests).zero?, "client remains admitted")
ensure
  begin
    cancellation.cancel
    waiting&.join
  ensure
    cancellation.close
  end
end
```
<!-- /example -->

## Async capture and cancellation

[Complete Async program](../examples/async_cancel.rb). A second task captures
while another tmux client waits; cancellation retires that client's process.

<!-- example: async_cancel/main -->
```ruby
Async do |parent|
  LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope|
    waiting = parent.async do
      scope.server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"], timeout: 0.5)
    rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error
      error
    end
    scope.server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 0.5)
    Example.check(scope.diagnostics.fetch(:active_process_slots) == 1, "waiting client lost its slot")
    captures = scope.map(scope.server.list_panes.map(&:ref), concurrency: 2) do |ref|
      scope.server.pane(ref).capture
    end
    Example.check(captures.all?(&:success?), "sibling captures stalled")
    waiting.cancel
    failure = waiting.wait
    Example.check(failure.is_a?(LibTmux::Cancelled), "cancellation lost")
    Example.check(failure.delivery == :possibly_sent, "cancelled dispatch claimed no effects")
    Example.raises(Errno::ECHILD) { Process.waitpid(failure.pid, Process::WNOHANG) }
    Example.check(scope.server.diagnostics.fetch(:admitted_requests).zero?, "cancelled client remains admitted")
  end
end.wait
```

## Control overflow

[Complete control program](../examples/control_overflow.rb). It needs tmux 3.7
or newer and demonstrates the refusal on older daemons. A slow reliable
subscriber fails explicitly; a tail subscriber reports a gap and replies
continue to drain.

<!-- example: control_overflow/main -->
```ruby
server.open_control(session: session.ref) do |control|
  control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 0.5)
  reliable = control.subscribe(max_events: 1, max_bytes: 1024)
  tail = control.subscribe(mode: :tail, max_events: 1, max_bytes: 1024)
  3.times { |index| window.rename("event#{index}") }
  reply = control.exchange("display-message -p alive", timeout: 0.5)
  Example.check(reply.blocks.last.body == "alive\n", "slow reader blocked commands")
  Example.check(reply.attribution == :boundary_window, "reply overclaims attribution")
  Example.check(reliable.diagnostics.fetch(:overflowed), "overflow is missing from diagnostics")
  Example.check(control.diagnostics.fetch(:retained_reply_bytes).zero?, "consumed reply remains retained")
  reliable.next(timeout: 0.5)
  Example.raises(LibTmux::SubscriptionOverflow) { reliable.next(timeout: 0.5) }
  gap = tail.next(timeout: 0.5)
  Example.check(gap.kind == :gap && gap.dropped_bytes.positive?, "tail hid lost bytes")
end
```

# libtmux Drive tmux from Ruby: [sessions][session], [windows][window] and [panes][pane] as handles, [snapshots][snapshot] you filter in plain Ruby, and [control connections][controlconnection] that report what tmux does. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/) [![libtmux](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux?label=libtmux)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux)
Part of [libtmux for Ruby](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby#readme). This gem is the core; the [packages below](#packages) build on it. [Create][server-new_session] and [split][pane-split] windows, [read][server-snapshot] and [filter][selection-where] what a server holds, and [type into a pane][pane-send_text] and capture what it shows. It suits scripts, tests that need a real tmux, and tools that drive a terminal program. [Cancel][cancellation-cancel] a request that is waiting, and [follow events][controlconnection-subscribe] as tmux emits them. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Find things](#find-sessions-windows-and-panes) · [Create](#create-sessions-windows-and-panes) · [Type and read](#type-into-a-pane-and-read-it-back) · [Your own server](#use-the-tmux-server-you-already-run) · [Cancel](#wait-time-out-and-cancel) · [Link windows](#link-a-window-into-several-sessions) · [Options](#read-and-set-options-and-hooks) · [Watch tmux](#watch-tmux-change) · [Groups](#run-several-commands-in-order) · [Packages](#packages) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer on `PATH`: ```console $ gem install libtmux ``` This program creates a session, adds a window, splits it, and prints each window with its panes. [`Server.start`][server-start] closes its private tmux server when the block exits, and the snapshot stays readable afterward: ```ruby require "libtmux" snapshot = LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window.split(direction: :horizontal, size: "40%", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.snapshot end snapshot.windows.each do |window| puts "#{window.name}: #{window.panes.map(&:id).join(', ')}" end ``` It prints: ```text main: %0 logs: %1, %2 ``` Requiring the gem starts no tmux process, scheduler or MCP server. [`Server.start`][server-start] gives its tmux server a socket and an empty configuration of its own, so it never touches a tmux you already use. ## Find sessions, windows, and panes ### [`Server#list_sessions`][server-list_sessions]: what tmux has now One call asks tmux for every session and returns frozen handles in numeric ID order. [`list_windows`][server-list_windows] and [`list_panes`][server-list_panes] are its siblings, and [`Session#list_windows`][session-list_windows] and [`Window#list_panes`][window-list_panes] narrow them: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) sessions = server.list_sessions puts "sessions: #{sessions.map(&:id).sort.join(', ')}" end ``` It runs on a private server and prints: ```text sessions: $0, $1 ``` An empty array means tmux answered with nothing to list. A listing that fails raises [`CommandError`][commanderror]. ### [`Server#snapshot`][server-snapshot]: one read, many queries Read the server once, then filter that read with [`where`][selection-where], [`select`][selection-select], [`one`][selection-one] and [`one_or_nil`][selection-one_or_nil]. These queries make no tmux calls. Continue with the snapshot from the quick start: ```ruby panes = snapshot.panes active_ids = panes.where(active: true).map(&:id) wide_panes = panes.select { |pane| pane.width >= 40 } panes_by_window = panes.group_by { |pane| pane.window.name } logs = snapshot.windows.one(name: "logs") missing = snapshot.windows.one_or_nil(name: "missing") ``` `one` raises [`NoMatchError`][nomatcherror] or [`MultipleMatchesError`][multiplematcheserror] unless exactly one record matches. `one_or_nil` returns `nil` for no match and still rejects duplicates. A selection keeps the membership it captured, so call `server.snapshot` again to read later changes. The [field catalog](../../docs/reference/fields.md) lists every query field and wire name. ### [`Server#search_panes`][server-search_panes]: the matching panes in one call `search_panes` captures the server and answers a selection of the panes whose fields match `where:`. [`explain_panes`][server-explain_panes] shows the plan without running tmux. This program also uses the snapshot queries above: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| work = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"], receipt: true) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) snapshot = server.snapshot session = snapshot.sessions.where(name: "work").one puts "matching session: #{session.name}" missing = snapshot.sessions.one_or_nil(name: "missing") puts "missing session: #{missing.nil?}" panes = server.search_panes(where: {id: work.pane.id}) puts "matching pane: #{panes.one.id}" end ``` It prints: ```text matching session: work missing session: true matching pane: %0 ``` ## Create sessions, windows, and panes ### [`Server#new_session`][server-new_session]: a session and its first window `new_session` starts a detached session that runs `command:`, an argv array. Ask for a receipt to read the IDs tmux assigned to the session, window and pane: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| created = server.new_session( name: "work", window_name: "main", command: ["/bin/cat"], receipt: true ) puts "session: #{created.entity.id}" puts "window: #{created.window.id}" puts "pane: #{created.pane.id}" end ``` It prints: ```text session: $0 window: @0 pane: %0 ``` Creation returns once tmux has assigned the IDs. It says nothing about whether the program started or exited cleanly. ### [`Session#new_window`][session-new_window]: add a window [`Pane#split`][pane-split] and [`Window#split`][window-split] add panes the same way. A new window takes a `name:` and the same `command:` as a session: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.new_window(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) puts "window: #{window.snapshot.name}" puts "session windows: #{session.list_windows.length}" end ``` It prints: ```text window: logs session windows: 2 ``` - `cwd:` names a directory on the machine running Ruby, and is checked before the command is sent. - `environment:` is a String-to-String map of literal values. - `new_window(index:)` refuses a slot that is taken. - [`Pane#split`][pane-split] targets that exact pane, and `size:` is a cell count or a percentage string such as `"40%"`. - New windows and splits keep focus unless you pass `focus: true`. The full contract is in [Creation][behavior-creation]. ## Type into a pane and read it back ### [`Pane#send_text`][pane-send_text]: type, then read what the pane showed `send_text` types literal text, and [`send_keys`][pane-send_keys] sends tmux key names such as `Enter`. [`Pane#capture`][pane-capture] reads the screen. To wait for output, poll the pane until the line appears. A [control connection][server-open_control] reports it as an event instead, but needs tmux 3.7 or newer: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| created = server.new_session( name: "capture", command: ["/bin/sh"], environment: {"ENV" => "/dev/null"}, receipt: true ) pane = created.pane pane.send_text("printf '\\nlibtmux capture ready\\n'") pane.send_keys("Enter") deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + 5 captured = pane.capture.stdout.lines(chomp: true) until captured.include?("libtmux capture ready") raise "Output did not arrive within five seconds" if Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline sleep 0.05 captured = pane.capture.stdout.lines(chomp: true) end raise "Expected output is absent from the pane" unless captured.include?("libtmux capture ready") puts "libtmux capture ready" end ``` It prints: ```text libtmux capture ready ``` - Sending input does not show that the shell finished the command. - `capture` returns the visible screen. `start:` and `finish:` choose a range, and `join:` joins wrapped lines. - `escapes:`, `escape_bytes:`, `preserve_trailing:` and `trim_trailing:` change the bytes it returns. - `mode_screen:`, `alternate:` and `pending:` read a copy-mode screen, the saved screen and an unfinished escape sequence. Pass at most one. - Binary buffers keep their trailing newlines. See [`write_buffer`][server-write_buffer] and [`read_buffer`][server-read_buffer] in the [layout and bytes recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#layout-and-bytes). The full contract is in [Pane input and capture][behavior-capture]. ## Use the tmux server you already run ### [`Server.new`][server-new]: borrow a daemon [`Server.open`][server-open] and [`Server.new`][server-new] bind an endpoint that already exists. Closing the binding retires its clients and leaves the daemon running; [`Server#kill`][server-kill] stops it. The outer [`Server.start`][server-start] block here only supplies a daemon to borrow: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |owner| owner.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server = LibTmux::Server.new(endpoint: owner.endpoint) begin puts "connected sessions: #{server.list_sessions.length}" ensure server.close end puts "sessions after client close: #{owner.list_sessions.length}" end ``` It prints: ```text connected sessions: 1 sessions after client close: 1 ``` - [`Endpoint.new`][endpoint-new] takes a socket path or socket name. With neither, it picks the socket tmux would: `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, `LIBTMUX_SOCKET`, the server `$TMUX` names, then tmux's default socket. [`Endpoint.from_env`][endpoint-from_env] follows `$TMUX` alone. - A binding keeps a private link to the socket it bound, so commands never reach a different daemon that later takes the same path. - A ref is valid on the server that issued it. Another server raises [`TargetNotFoundError`][targetnotfounderror]. See [ownership and errors](../../docs/ownership-errors.md). ## Wait, time out, and cancel ### [`Cancellation.new`][cancellation-new]: wake a request that is waiting Typed operations take `timeout:` and `cancel:`. Pass a [`Cancellation`][cancellation] token as `cancel:`, call [`cancel`][cancellation-cancel] from another thread to wake the request, join its callers, then [`close`][cancellation-close] the token: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) cancellation = LibTmux::Cancellation.new waiting = Thread.new do server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"], timeout: 5, cancel: cancellation) rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error error end server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 5) cancellation.cancel failure = waiting.value puts "request: #{failure.class}" puts "delivery: #{failure.delivery}" cancellation.close end ``` It prints: ```text request: LibTmux::Cancelled delivery: possibly_sent ``` [`Cancelled`][cancelled] reports `delivery` as `:not_sent` or `:possibly_sent`. Cancelling does not undo what tmux already queued. The [plain-Ruby recipe](../../examples/cancel.rb) also checks that the client was reaped. The contracts are in [Cancellation tokens][behavior-cancellation] and [ownership and errors](../../docs/ownership-errors.md). ## Link a window into several sessions ### [`Session#link_window`][session-link_window]: one window at several indexes A [`WindowLink`][windowlink] keeps a session, an index and a window ID together, so a window linked twice stays one window. `link_window` needs an explicit `index:`: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "links", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) session.link_window(window.ref, index: 4) session.link_window(window.ref, index: 9) links = session.list_window_links puts "indexes: #{links.map(&:index).join(', ')}" puts "windows: #{links.map { |link| link.window.id }.uniq.join(', ')}" end ``` It prints: ```text indexes: 0, 4, 9 windows: @0 ``` - Select, unlink, move, swap and display check the whole link identity in the same tmux queue turn as the operation. - A hook that waits before dispatch cannot turn a stale link into its replacement. - Rewriting command aliases during an operation is outside that guarantee, so coordinate configuration changes. The contract is in [Window links][behavior-window-links], and the [linked-windows recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#one-window-at-three-indexes) runs this at three indexes. ## Read and set options and hooks ### [`Session#options`][session-options]: a value with its inheritance [`Options#set`][options-set] writes an option at the scope of its accessor. [`Options#get`][options-get] reads it back as an [`OptionValue`][optionvalue], and [`as`][optionvalue-as] converts it strictly. [`Hooks#set`][hooks-set] stores a tmux command: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) session.options.set("history-limit", 5000) limit = session.options.get("history-limit") puts "history-limit: #{limit.as(:integer)}" puts "inherited: #{limit.inherited?}" session.hooks.set("after-new-window", command: "display-message created") puts "hook: #{session.hooks.get('after-new-window').as(:string)}" end ``` It prints: ```text history-limit: 5000 inherited: false hook: display-message created ``` - An [`OptionValue`][optionvalue] keeps the raw bytes, whether the value is inherited, and the array index. `as` takes `:bytes`, `:string`, `:integer` or `:boolean`. - A missing array index raises [`NoMatchError`][nomatcherror], and a present empty value stays present. - Reading an array without an index raises [`MultipleMatchesError`][multiplematcheserror] when it has several entries. - Hook values stay tmux command strings, and indexed hooks run in index order. The contracts are in [Options and hooks][behavior-options] and [Option values][behavior-option-values]. ## Watch tmux change ### [`Server#open_control`][server-open_control]: events as they happen A [`ControlConnection`][controlconnection] runs a command with [`exchange`][controlconnection-exchange] and streams what tmux reports through [`subscribe`][controlconnection-subscribe]. The subscription's [`next`][controlsubscription-next] waits for the next [`ControlEvent`][controlevent]: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) server.open_control(session: session.ref) do |control| reply = control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 5) puts "reply: #{reply.blocks.last.body.strip}" events = control.subscribe(max_events: 64, max_bytes: 65_536) window.rename("renamed") event = events.next(timeout: 5) until event&.raw&.start_with?("%window-renamed") puts "event: #{event.raw.strip}" end end ``` It prints: ```text reply: ready event: %window-renamed @0 renamed ``` - `exchange` answers a [`GuardedReply`][guardedreply]. It holds the blocks seen between two boundaries, and a hook can print into the same interval. - A subscription is bounded. A reliable one raises [`SubscriptionOverflow`][subscriptionoverflow] when it falls behind, and a tail one reports the lost range as a `:gap` event. - [`pause_output`][controlconnection-pause_output] and [`resume_output`][controlconnection-resume_output] return a [`GuardedReply`][guardedreply]. A reply does not show that the action took effect. - To reconnect, close the old connection and pass it as `open_control(session: ref, reconnect: old_connection)`. The replacement has a new `generation`, and every new subscription starts with a `:reconnect` gap. Nothing is replayed. The contracts are in [Control connections][behavior-control], and the [control overflow recipe](../../docs/recipes.md#control-overflow) runs both subscription modes. ## Run several commands in order ### [`Server#run_group`][server-run_group]: several commands through one client A group submits several tmux commands in order through one client. The [`GroupResult`][groupresult] holds one aggregate status, and each step reports `unknown`: ```ruby require "libtmux" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) group = server.run_group([ ["set-option", "-g", "@before", "kept"], ["select-pane", "-t", "%4294967294"], ["set-option", "-g", "@after", "never run"] ]) puts "success: #{group.success?}" puts "steps: #{group.steps.map { |step| step.fetch(:outcome) }.join(', ')}" puts "@before: #{server.options(scope: :session).get('@before').as(:string)}" end ``` It prints: ```text success: false steps: unknown, unknown, unknown @before: kept ``` The first command keeps its effect when the second fails, and the third never runs. # libtmux-async Run libtmux operations inside an application-owned Async task: a [subprocess facade][async-server], [ordered mapping][async-scope-map], [control replies][guardedreply] and [event subscriptions][async-controlsubscription]. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/reference/libtmux-async/) · [Guide](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/guides/async/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/) [![libtmux-async](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-async?label=libtmux-async)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-async)
Part of [libtmux for Ruby](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby#readme). Built on [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux). Imports start no scheduler, tmux server or background task. A scope borrows a core [`Server`][server] and leaves its daemon running when the scope exits. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Cancel](#cancel-a-request-without-stalling-the-others) · [Map](#keep-results-ordered-and-bounded) · [Control](#read-control-events-in-a-scope) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer on `PATH`: ```console $ gem install libtmux-async ``` Open a scope over a core server with [`LibTmux::Async.open`][async-open], then capture every pane concurrently with [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]. The outer [`Server.start`][server-start] block only supplies a server for the scope to borrow: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) server.new_session(name: "logs", command: ["/bin/cat"]) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| refs = scope.server.list_panes.map(&:ref) screens = scope.map(refs, concurrency: 2) { |ref| scope.server.pane(ref).capture } puts "captured panes: #{screens.length}" puts "all succeeded: #{screens.all?(&:success?)}" end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text captured panes: 2 all succeeded: true ``` - Leave out `parent:` to use the current Async task. - A scope rejects use from another thread, process or scheduler, so create one scope for each scheduler thread. - Scope exit retires its clients and joins its owned tasks. ## Cancel a request without stalling the others ### [`Async::Server#run`][async-server-run]: cancel a request that is waiting `scope.server.run` waits for a tmux command in a task. Cancel that task and the scope retires its client, while sibling requests keep running. [`wait_for`][async-server-wait_for] returns once the request has signalled that it is running, so the cancel arrives while it waits: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| waiting = parent.async do scope.server.run(["wait-for", "-S", "ready", ";", "wait-for", "held"], timeout: 5) rescue LibTmux::Cancelled => error error end scope.server.wait_for("ready", timeout: 5) waiting.cancel failure = waiting.wait puts "request: #{failure.class}" puts "delivery: #{failure.delivery}" end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text request: LibTmux::Cancelled delivery: possibly_sent ``` - `run` returns the same binary [`CommandResult`][commandresult] as the core. - [`Cancelled`][cancelled] carries `delivery` as `:not_sent` or `:possibly_sent`. A deadline cannot undo tmux effects. - Interactive terminal attachment stays on the blocking core and raises [`UnsupportedFeatureError`][unsupportedfeatureerror] here. The [complete program](../../examples/async_cancel.rb) also keeps capturing while the request waits, and checks that the cancelled client is reaped. The contract is in [Async scope][behavior-async-scope]. ## Keep results ordered and bounded ### [`Scope#map`][async-scope-map]: input order, capped payloads `map` runs a block for each item, up to `concurrency:` at a time, and returns a frozen Array in input order. The quick start is a `map`. These limits apply to every scope: | Scope limit | Default | | --- | --- | | Active subprocess clients | 4 | | Admitted subprocess requests, including unconsumed results | 32 | | Queued request payload | 4 MiB | | Retained process and map output payload | 8 MiB | | Per-command stdout / stderr | 1 MiB / 256 KiB | | Control connections | 4 | | Ordinary command deadline | 5 seconds | - Independent requests may complete out of order, and the result is still in input order. - `map` caps retained items and counts payload bytes of strings, primitive values, [`CommandResult`][commandresult], Arrays and Hashes. Cycles and deep nesting are refused. - An application-defined result needs a `result_bytes:` callable that returns a nonnegative Integer. - Keep measured values unchanged until the map returns. The counts cover payload bytes and do not measure the Ruby heap. The contract is in [Async map][behavior-async-map]. ## Read control events in a scope ### [`Async::Server#open_control`][async-server-open_control]: replies and events A control connection has its own request, reply and subscriber limits. [`exchange`][async-controlconnection-exchange] runs one command, and [`events`][async-controlconnection-events] yields what tmux reports outside a reply: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/async" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| session = server.new_session(name: "work", command: ["/bin/cat"]) window = session.list_windows.fetch(0) Async do |parent| LibTmux::Async.open(parent: parent, server: server) do |scope| scope.server.open_control(session: session.ref) do |control| reply = control.exchange("display-message -p ready", timeout: 5) puts "reply: #{reply.blocks.last.body.strip}" events = control.events window.rename("renamed") event = events.next(timeout: 5) until event&.raw&.start_with?("%window-renamed") puts "event: #{event.raw.strip}" end end end.wait end ``` It prints: ```text reply: ready event: %window-renamed @0 renamed ``` - `exchange` answers a [`GuardedReply`][guardedreply] with `:boundary_window` attribution. It makes no claim that the command finished. - Events arrive through `events.next` or an explicit [`subscribe`][async-controlconnection-subscribe]. Consumer callbacks run outside the parser. - A reliable subscription raises on overflow, and a tail subscription reports the dropped range. - Cancelling a dispatched exchange that is not drained closes the connection. - [`pause_output`][async-controlconnection-pause_output] and [`resume_output`][async-controlconnection-resume_output] report possible loss through gap events. A gap does not show that the action took effect. - To reconnect, close the connection and pass it as `reconnect:`. The replacement stays owned by the scope, has a new generation, and starts with a gap of unknown loss. Nothing is replayed. The contract is in [Control connections][behavior-control]. ## What it leaves out - **Terminal attachment.** `attach` stays on the blocking core and raises [`UnsupportedFeatureError`][unsupportedfeatureerror] on this facade. - **Replay.** Reconnect and resume never replay requests or missed output. See [Execution modes][doc-modes]. - **Cross-thread scopes.** A scope belongs to the thread, process and scheduler that opened it. # libtmux-mcp Expose an existing tmux server over MCP stdio. Read snapshots, capture pane output and wait for events, or enable creation, input and shell commands one tool at a time. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/reference/) · [Tools](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/) [![libtmux-mcp](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-mcp?label=libtmux-mcp)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-mcp)
Part of [libtmux for Ruby](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby#readme). Built on [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux) and [libtmux-async](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux-async). An MCP client starts `libtmux-mcp` and talks to it over stdin and stdout. The official MCP SDK handles the protocol, and bounded Async tasks handle transport. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Connect a client](#connect-a-client) · [Choose the server](#choose-which-tmux-server-it-serves) · [The tools](#the-tools) · [Read](#read-the-layout-and-the-screen) · [Create](#create-type-and-close) · [Run](#run-a-script-in-a-pane) · [Embed](#embed-it-in-ruby) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem and its `libtmux-mcp` executable. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer and tmux 3.3a or newer: ```console $ gem install libtmux-mcp ``` The server borrows a tmux server that is already running. Start one on a socket of its own: ```console $ tmux -L agent new-session -d -s work ``` Add the server to Claude Code. Until you enable more tools, it serves [`tmux_capabilities`][tool-tmux_capabilities] and [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: ```console $ claude mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp --socket-name agent --endpoint dev ``` Run by hand, `libtmux-mcp` waits for input until EOF. `libtmux-mcp --help` lists every option. ## Connect a client ### `claude mcp add`: Claude Code The command in the quick start registers the server with Claude Code. Start the tmux server first, as above. ### `codex mcp add`: Codex CLI Codex CLI takes the same command after `--`: ```console $ codex mcp add tmux -- libtmux-mcp --socket-name agent --endpoint dev ``` ### `mcpServers`: clients that read JSON A client that reads a JSON configuration, such as Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`, takes the same command as an `mcpServers` entry: ```json { "mcpServers": { "tmux": { "command": "libtmux-mcp", "args": ["--socket-name", "agent", "--endpoint", "dev"] } } } ``` If the client does not start servers with your shell's `PATH`, set `command` to the absolute path that `command -v libtmux-mcp` prints. ## Choose which tmux server it serves ### `--socket` and `--socket-name`: pick the daemon Set `TMUX_SOCKET` to an existing tmux socket. This command borrows that daemon and serves MCP on stdin and stdout: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket "$TMUX_SOCKET" \ --endpoint local ``` Use `--socket-name NAME` instead of `--socket PATH` to select a named socket, as the quick start does: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent ``` - With neither flag, the server borrows the socket in `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, else the name in `LIBTMUX_SOCKET`, else the server `TMUX` names when it runs inside tmux, else tmux's default socket. When both variables are set, the path wins, and an empty variable counts as unset. A flag ignores both variables, and the two flags are refused together. - The server never starts a tmux server. When none answers at the socket it chose, it exits with status 1. - Started from a tmux pane with no flag or variable, the server drives that pane's server. Pass `--socket-name` to give an agent a server of its own. - EOF retires the clients the server owns and leaves the daemon running. - `--endpoint` sets the public alias in discovery and resource URIs, and defaults to `local`. ## The tools Each tool name links to its page on libtmux.org, with the arguments, limits and result schema. Repeat `--enable-tool` for each additional tool. | Tools | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | [`tmux_capabilities`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_capabilities/), [`tmux_snapshot`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_snapshot/) | Enabled | Discover capabilities and query captured metadata | | [`tmux_capture`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_capture/), [`tmux_wait`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_wait/) | Disabled | Capture a screen or wait for text/process exit | | [`tmux_create`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_create/), [`tmux_send`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_send/), [`tmux_close`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_close/) | Disabled | Create entities, send text/keys and tear down exact targets | | [`tmux_run`](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/mcp/tools/tmux_run/) | Disabled | Run a script in an explicitly enrolled zsh shell | - Disabled tools are absent from discovery and denied on direct application calls. - An unknown tool name is refused when the server starts. The [complete protocol recipe](../../examples/mcp_protocol.rb) exercises discovery, snapshots, default denial, enabled mutations, cancellation and EOF cleanup through actual pipes, including the installed executable. ## Read the layout and the screen ### [`tmux_snapshot`][tool-tmux_snapshot]: the layout, in pages - Pages come from one immutable capture, and a cursor continues that capture. - An expired, evicted or foreign cursor returns an error. The server never substitutes a fresh listing. ### [`tmux_capture`][tool-tmux_capture]: a pane's screen Enable the screen tools together: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket "$TMUX_SOCKET" \ --enable-tool tmux_capture \ --enable-tool tmux_wait ``` - It reads a bounded screen and keeps its line endings. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 come back base64-encoded. - With tracking, a call returns a cursor, and later calls return a splice against that exact captured state. A cursor from another server generation or from a respawned pane is refused. - It refuses a pane whose effective `after-capture-pane` hook is not empty, including inherited entries. - On tmux 3.3a to 3.4 the hook is checked before the capture command runs, so keep hook configuration stable while observing. ### [`tmux_wait`][tool-tmux_wait]: wait for text or exit - It waits for screen text, or for the pane process to exit. Screen text comes from control events on tmux 3.7 and newer, and from polling the pane every 50 ms on older daemons, which take no control client. Process exit uses process descriptors. - Wrapped rows are joined, so text that the pane width split across rows still matches. - If the pane, or the tmux server holding it, ends before the text appears, the call fails with `pane_died`, `delivery: observed` and the last rows it read in the error's `capture`. If only the control stream ends while the pane lives, such as after the client detaches, the failure is `observation_lost`. - A cancelled or expired wait closes its observers and never signals the pane program. - Process tracking needs a native identity backend: Linux peer pidfds with matching PID namespaces, or Darwin kqueue. Without one, the call is refused. ### [Resource templates][mcp-resources]: the same data as URIs [`tmux_metadata`][resource-tmux_metadata], [`tmux_metadata_page`][resource-tmux_metadata_page] and [`tmux_screen`][resource-tmux_screen] expose metadata pages and pane screens under endpoint and generation URIs, with the same policy and limits as their tools. - The server does not advertise resource subscriptions. - [Snapshots, cursors and references][mcp-snapshots-topic] has the full contract. ## Create, type and close ### [`tmux_create`][tool-tmux_create]: new sessions, windows and panes Enable the three tools together: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --enable-tool tmux_create \ --enable-tool tmux_send \ --enable-tool tmux_close ``` - It takes argument arrays as `argv`. - Results carry the references tmux returned. ### [`tmux_send`][tool-tmux_send]: literal text or named keys - Text and keys are separate variants. - It reports `dispatch_only`: the input was dispatched, and the command has not necessarily finished. - After a cancellation, the effect stays unknown and is not reported as none. ### [`tmux_close`][tool-tmux_close]: an exact target - It takes an exact session, window or pane reference, and never selects by name. ## Run a script in a pane ### [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run]: authored commands in an enrolled zsh [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run] runs a POSIX script in a pane's interactive zsh 5.9. It needs both the tool and an enrolled pane. List the pane IDs of the server: ```console $ tmux -L agent list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}' ``` ```text %0 ``` Enable the tool and write a setup file for one exact pane: ```console $ libtmux-mcp \ --socket-name agent \ --enable-tool tmux_run \ --enroll-pane %0=enroll.zsh ``` Then, in that pane's zsh, run `source enroll.zsh`. A relative path resolves from the directory where the server starts. - `--enroll-pane` requires `--enable-tool tmux_run`, and each pane and each file may appear once. - The server writes a private file (mode `0600`) and never types into the terminal. It refuses an existing file or a symlink. - Setup files expire. `--enrollment-timeout SECONDS` sets the lifetime, at most 300. - EOF retires pending enrollment and removes only the files the server wrote. - A call takes an exact pane `target`, a POSIX `script`, and optional `stdout_limit` and `stderr_limit` byte counts. - The script runs with the shell's working directory and exported environment. - Stdout and stderr come back separately, as UTF-8 or base64. - A nonzero exit or a signal is a completion result. Output over its limit is an error with completion unobserved, and never a truncated success. - Cancelling a run does not prove that its child processes stopped. ## Embed it in Ruby Require `libtmux/mcp`. Imports start no tmux process, scheduler or MCP server. The [execution guide](../../docs/modes.md) covers result and ownership boundaries. ### [`LibTmux::MCP::Application`][mcp-application]: serve from your own program [`Application`][mcp-application] borrows an application-owned [`LibTmux::Async::Server`][async-server]. Its [`sdk_server`][mcp-application-sdk_server] supplies the SDK server that [`StdioTransport`][mcp-stdiotransport] consumes: ```ruby application = LibTmux::MCP::Application.new(server: scope.server, endpoint_name: "example") sdk = application.sdk_server input, client_input = IO.pipe client_output, output = IO.pipe transport = LibTmux::MCP::StdioTransport.new(server: sdk, parent: parent, input: input, output: output) runner = parent.async { transport.run } ``` The [complete program](../../examples/mcp_protocol.rb) runs this excerpt inside an Async task with an open [`LibTmux::Async`][async] scope. It sends real JSON-RPC messages through the pipes, checks the replies, and prints `PASS mcp_protocol`. ### [`Application#invite_shell`][mcp-application-invite_shell]: enroll a shell from Ruby Call `invite_shell` with a pane reference, `timeout:` and `expires_in:`, then pass the invitation to [`accept_shell`][mcp-application-accept_shell]. - The invitation's `shell_arguments` make up the setup command to source in that pane's zsh. - `timeout:` bounds acquisition, and `expires_in:` sets the enrollment lifetime. - The application owns invitations and accepted connections until [`close`][mcp-application-close]. Direct enrollment calls enforce tool policy. ## What it leaves out - **Tools you have not enabled.** Disabled tools are absent from discovery, and a direct application call is denied. See [The tools](#the-tools). - **Resource subscriptions.** The server does not advertise them. See the [resource templates][mcp-resources]. - **Typing into your terminal.** The server writes a private setup file and never types into a pane's terminal to enroll it. See [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run]. - **A guaranteed stop.** Cancelling a run does not prove that its child processes stopped. See [`tmux_run`][tool-tmux_run]. ## Support and status Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and each release increments `N`. The API is not settled: any release may change or remove exported identifiers, and the changelogs mark each break. Pin an exact version to avoid one. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and the [main changelog](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for changes that span gems. - **Ruby 3.3 or newer.** The gem depends on `libtmux` and `libtmux-async` at the same version, the `mcp` SDK 1.5, `digest` and `optparse`. - **tmux 3.3a or newer.** The server refuses an older daemon when it starts, before it serves any tool, and prints the reason and the remedy on stderr. - **A daemon that changes while it runs.** A tool call returns an `unsupported` result with `delivery: not_sent`. The result names the floor and says to upgrade tmux and restart the server. - **The `screen_contains` wait.** It uses control events on tmux 3.7 and newer and polls the pane screen on older daemons, which take no control client. - **Linux, including WSL, and macOS.** The core [compatibility workflow][compat] runs Ruby 3.3, 3.4 and 4.0 with tmux 3.3a through 3.8 on Ubuntu 24.04. A push and a pull request run the oldest and newest of those releases, 3.3a and 3.8, and a release runs all of them. macOS is supported on a best-effort basis, and CI coverage for it is highly
