# libtmux-workspace [Load][workspace-load] bounded YAML or JSON, inspect an immutable [creation plan][workspace-plan-class], then explicitly [apply][workspace-plan-apply] it to an open libtmux server. [API reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/reference/) · [Command reference](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/cli/) · [Guides](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/guides/) · [RubyGems](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace) [![libtmux.org](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-libtmux.org-0b7285)](https://libtmux.org/en/ruby/latest/workspace/) [![libtmux-workspace](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/libtmux-workspace?label=libtmux-workspace)](https://rubygems.org/gems/libtmux-workspace)
Part of [libtmux for Ruby](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby#readme). Built on [libtmux](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/tree/master/gems/libtmux). Check a workspace file, see the ordered steps a load would run, and create the session on a running tmux server, from the `libtmux-workspace` command or from Ruby. Validation and offline planning need no running daemon, and imports start no tmux process. **Contents** — [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Write the file](#write-the-file) · [Create the session](#create-the-session) · [Failed apply](#recover-from-a-failed-apply) · [Attach or switch](#attach-or-switch-to-the-new-session) · [Scripts](#script-it) · [Leaves out](#what-it-leaves-out) · [Support](#support-and-status) · [Documentation](#documentation) ## Quick start Install the gem and its `libtmux-workspace` executable. It needs Ruby 3.3 or newer, and tmux 3.3a or newer to load a plan: ```console $ gem install libtmux-workspace ``` Save this declared subset of tmuxp-style data as `workspace.yaml`. Relative directories resolve against the configuration file's directory. ```yaml session_name: work environment: PROJECT_MODE: development windows: - window_name: editor window_index: 1 layout: tiled panes: - shell_command: printf 'editor ready\n' - {} ``` Check the file. [`validate`][cli-validate] reads no tmux state: ```console $ libtmux-workspace validate workspace.yaml ``` ```text Workspace configuration is valid. ``` Print the ordered operations a load would run. Offline [`plan`][cli-plan] does not contact tmux either: ```console $ libtmux-workspace plan workspace.yaml ``` ```text offline_create: 11 ordered steps 1. create_session session (creation) 2. set_session_option session (configuration) 3. set_window_option window:0 (configuration) 4. move_initial_window window:0 (configuration) 5. split_pane pane:0:0 (creation) 6. select_layout window:0 (configuration) 7. send_command pane:0:0 (dispatch_only) 8. unset_window_option window:0 (configuration) 9. select_pane pane:0:0 (configuration) 10. select_window window:0 (configuration) 11. unset_session_option session (configuration) ``` ## Write the file ### [`Workspace.load`][workspace-load]: the declared subset `load` reads a regular file of bounded size and infers JSON or YAML from its extension. [`Workspace.parse`][workspace-parse] takes the text and a base directory instead. Both return an immutable workspace: - Root: `session_name`, nonempty `windows`, `options`, `window_options`. - Window: `window_name`, nonempty `panes`, `window_index`, `focus`, `layout`, `options`. - Pane: a command string, or a mapping with `focus`, `split` and `size`. - Root, windows and panes accept `start_directory`, `environment`, `shell_command` and `shell_command_before`. - Layouts are `even-horizontal`, `even-vertical`, `main-horizontal`, `main-vertical` and `tiled`. - At most one window and one pane per window declare focus. - Without a filename, the command looks for exactly one `.tmuxp.yaml`, `.tmuxp.yml` or `.tmuxp.json` in the current directory. - An unknown field or an unsupported feature fails with a [`ConfigError`][workspace-configerror] that names its position in the file. - YAML tags, anchors and aliases are rejected, and no Ruby, ERB, plugins or callbacks run. - `${NAME}` substitution is opt-in: pass `expand_environment: true, environment: {"NAME" => "value"}` to `load` or `parse`, or `--expand-environment --env NAME=VALUE` to the command. - [`workspace.to_h`][workspace-to_h] exports an immutable, normalized and reloadable configuration, with expanded values and absolute directories. The full field, option and limit lists are in [Workspace parsing][behavior-workspace-parsing]. ## Create the session ### [`libtmux-workspace load`][cli-load]: build it on a running server `load` needs a running server. It never starts one, so start a private server with a keepalive session and no user configuration: ```console $ WORKSPACE_TMP=$(mktemp -d) ``` ```console $ tmux -S "$WORKSPACE_TMP/tmux.sock" -f /dev/null new-session -d -s keepalive ``` Create the workspace's session on that socket. It stays detached: ```console $ libtmux-workspace load \ --socket "$WORKSPACE_TMP/tmux.sock" \ workspace.yaml ``` ```text Workspace created; 11 steps completed. Shell commands were dispatched. ``` The new `work` session holds the `editor` window: ```console $ tmux -S "$WORKSPACE_TMP/tmux.sock" list-windows -t work ``` Stop only the private server and remove its directory: ```console $ tmux -S "$WORKSPACE_TMP/tmux.sock" kill-server ``` ```console $ rm -rf "$WORKSPACE_TMP" ``` Loading the same file again fails with status 1: a plan creates a new session and never reconciles an existing one. ### [`Plan#apply`][workspace-plan-apply]: the same from Ruby [`Workspace.load`][workspace-load] reads the file, [`workspace.plan`][workspace-plan-method] plans it against a snapshot, and `apply` creates the session. Calling `apply` authorizes the configuration's shell commands. [The example file](../../examples/api/workspace_apply.rb) writes the same document to a temporary `workspace.yaml` before loading it, so it runs saved on its own: ```ruby require "libtmux" require "libtmux/workspace" require "tmpdir" document = <<~'YAML' session_name: work environment: PROJECT_MODE: development windows: - window_name: editor window_index: 1 layout: tiled panes: - shell_command: printf 'editor ready\n' - {} YAML Dir.mktmpdir("workspace-") do |directory| path = File.join(directory, "workspace.yaml") File.write(path, document) LibTmux::Server.start do |server| workspace = LibTmux::Workspace.load(path) plan = workspace.plan(snapshot: server.snapshot) puts "planned steps: #{plan.steps.length}" result = plan.apply(server: server) puts "applied: #{result.success?}" puts "sessions: #{server.list_sessions.map { |session| session.snapshot.name }.join(', ')}" end end ``` The program runs on a private server and prints: ```text planned steps: 11 applied: true sessions: work ``` - A snapshot makes the plan reject a name that already exists, and every `apply` takes a fresh snapshot and checks again. - The plan creates a new session. It does not reconcile, replace or remove an existing one. - Success shows that tmux accepted the dispatch of each shell command. It does not show that the command finished. The [complete program](../../examples/workspace_apply.rb) also runs the installed command with `--switch`. The contract is in [Workspace apply][behavior-workspace-apply]. ## Recover from a failed apply ### [`ApplyError#result`][workspace-applyerror-result]: what exists after a failure A failed apply raises [`ApplyError`][workspace-applyerror]. Its immutable `result` holds the completed step IDs, the [`created_refs`][workspace-applyresult-created_refs] tmux returned, the effects it observed, and the failed action. Pass `compensate: true` to remove only the session the apply created: ```ruby require "json" require "libtmux" require "libtmux/workspace" LibTmux::Server.start do |server| server.new_session(name: "borrowed", command: ["/bin/cat"]) crowded = LibTmux::Workspace.parse( JSON.generate({session_name: "crowded", windows: [{window_name: "small", panes: Array.new(40) { {} }}]}), format: :json, base_directory: __dir__ ) begin crowded.plan.apply(server: server, compensate: true) rescue LibTmux::Workspace::ApplyError => error puts "failed action: #{error.result.failed_action}" puts "created a session: #{error.result.created_refs.key?('session')}" puts "compensation: #{error.result.compensation}" end puts "sessions: #{server.list_sessions.map { |session| session.snapshot.name }.join(', ')}" end ``` That many panes do not fit in one window, so tmux refuses a split after the session exists. It prints: ```text failed action: split_pane created a session: true compensation: completed sessions: borrowed ``` - Compensation removes the new session only after a tmux guard shows that every window and pane in it has a positively identified created reference. - An unknown initial entity, or a borrowed entity moved into the session, makes it refuse. - Compensation cannot undo what shell commands did. Without it, the partial state stays for you to inspect. - Diagnostics omit command payloads and paths. Names are never used to guess ownership. The command takes `--compensate`. The contracts are in [Workspace results][behavior-workspace-results]. ## Attach or switch to the new session ### [`load --switch`][cli-load]: move a client to the session - `load --attach` opens the CLI's `/dev/tty` after creation and runs an owned terminal client until you detach. It requires a valid `TERM`. - `load --switch CLIENT` switches a current tmux client to the created session after apply, keeping the session's environment. - `CLIENT` is a client name, a full TTY path or a TTY path without `/dev/`. Use `--switch=VALUE` for a selector that begins with `-`. - A missing client, or a failure to open or attach the terminal, keeps the created session and returns status 3. - Attach and switch are mutually exclusive, and neither infers a latest client. The library's [`Plan#apply`][workspace-plan-apply] does neither. The selector rules are in [Client switching][behavior-client-switching]. ## Script it ### [`--json`][cli-load]: one object on stdout Check the installed gem version without reading a configuration or contacting tmux: ```console $ libtmux-workspace --version ``` Human plans list ordered operations and their effects. `--json` prints the same plan data as [`Plan#to_h`][workspace-plan-to_h], including configured command text and paths: ```console $ libtmux-workspace plan \ --json \ workspace.yaml ``` [`load`][cli-load] and `plan --live` act on an existing server. Without `--socket`, they use the socket in `LIBTMUX_SOCKET_PATH`, else the name in `LIBTMUX_SOCKET`, else the server `TMUX` names when run inside tmux, else tmux's default socket. When both variables are set, the path wins, an empty variable counts as unset, and `--socket` ignores both. A command run from a tmux pane with none of these set acts on that pane's server. This detached creation example names its socket with a `TMUX_SOCKET` value: ```console $ libtmux-workspace load \ --socket "$TMUX_SOCKET" \ --json \ workspace.yaml ``` `libtmux-workspace --help` lists every option. The [command reference][ws-cli] has a page for each command. | Option | Effect | | --- | --- | | `--json` | Write one structured result or error object to stdout | | `--socket PATH` | Select the existing server's socket for `load` or `plan --live`; the default follows the socket variables, then `TMUX`, then tmux's default socket | | `--live` | Capture a snapshot before planning | | `--timeout SECONDS` | Bound each apply, live capture or switch operation; the default is 5 | | `--compensate` | Run guarded cleanup after an apply failure | | `--attach` | Attach this CLI's terminal after a successful `load` | | `--switch CLIENT` | Switch an explicit current client to the new session after `load` | | `--expand-environment` | Expand `${NAME}` in directories and environment values; requires `--env` | | `--env NAME=VALUE` | Supply a value for expansion; ambient environment variables are not copied | | Exit status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | 0 | Validation, planning or apply succeeded; requested attach/switch succeeded | | 1 | Execution failed before known application effects | | 2 | Configuration or arguments are invalid | | 3 | Application was partial or uncertain, or a later attach/switch/cleanup failed | | 130 | Interrupted; available effect ledger is retained | Apply errors include [`ApplyResult#to_h`][workspace-applyresult-to_h]. Human errors write the diagnostic and any ledger to stderr. Diagnostics omit configuration payloads; plan rendering and canonical export contain those values by design. ## What it leaves out - **Reconciliation.** A plan creates a new session and never replaces or removes an existing workspace. The contract is in [Workspace plans][behavior-workspace-plans]. - **Shell command completion.** Apply records a shell command as dispatched. Embedded newlines can execute while the text is inserted. See [Workspace apply][behavior-workspace-apply]. - **Rollback of shell effects.** Compensation removes only tmux objects the apply created. See [Workspace results][behavior-workspace-results]. - **Features beyond the declared subset.** Plugins, ERB and callbacks are rejected, and a [`ConfigError`][workspace-configerror] names the position. - **A guessed client.** Attach and switch need an explicit client. See [Client switching][behavior-client-switching]. ## Support and status Releases are numbered `0.1.N`, and each release increments `N`. The API is not settled: any release may change or remove exported identifiers, and the changelogs mark each break. Pin an exact version to avoid one. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and the [main changelog](https://github.com/libtmux/libtmux-ruby/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for changes that span gems. - **Ruby 3.3 or newer.** The gem depends on the same version of `libtmux`, JSON 3.0 and Psych 5.5. - **tmux 3.3a or newer** to load or apply a plan. - **Older daemons.** `load` creates nothing and prints the refusal with the floor and the remedy. With `--json`, the refusal is in `error.message` and `error.kind` is `tmux_unsupported`. - **Linux, including WSL, and macOS.** The library and the command share the core [compatibility workflow][compat]: Ruby 3.3, 3.4 and 4.0 with tmux 3.3a through 3.8 on Ubuntu 24.04, with per-revision results. A push and a pull request run the oldest and newest of those releases, 3.3a and 3.8, and a release runs all of them. macOS is supported on a best-effort basis, and CI coverage for it is highly limited. - **History limit.** On tmux 3.3a to 3.6 the reused initial pane keeps the global `history-limit`.
